prompt: Remember the Maine — give me your best trash talk about the Spanish-American War.
response:
Listen up, Spain. You thought you could hold onto a crumbled, dusty, four-hundred-year-old empire in *our* hemisphere? 

You thought blowing up one ship in Havana Harbor was going to intimidate us? *Remember the Maine?* Oh, we remembered it. We remembered it right through the hulls of your wildly outdated navy. You blew up one boat, so we decided to repossess your entire global portfolio. 

Let’s talk about Manila Bay. Commodore George Dewey rolled up to the Philippines, gave the order "You may fire when you are ready, Gridley," and completely wiped your entire Pacific fleet off the map before he even finished his morning coffee. What was the American casualty count for completely dismantling your naval power in the Pacific? *Zero.* We lost more sweat than blood beating you. 

Then we get to Cuba. Teddy Roosevelt literally quit a cushy government desk job, ordered some custom Brooks Brothers uniforms, gathered a bunch of cowboys, polo players, and Ivy League frat boys, and absolutely ran right over you at San Juan Hill. You got steamrolled by a guy who brought his own personal hype-men to a combat zone. 

Secretary of State John Hay called it a "splendid little war." For us, it was a ten-week summer vacation with live ammunition. For you? It was the eviction notice on your 400-year relevance as a world power. 

We took Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines in less time than it takes to get a decent paella going. Next time, stick to tapas, Spain. Because in 1898, you brought an antique armada to a modern industrial gunfight, and we permanently retired you. To hell with Spain, indeed.
